{"notes": "Visit 2 (2:45). The table now shows a connected fish. Every domino is dark, so top and bottom lines both link to the start with no pale pieces. The nose splits cleanly, and both bodies curve to the right and finish in S-curves. The tail is NOT closed: the top arm ends near (28.3, 5.9) and the bottom arm near (26.3, 15.3), with a large gap between them. I can't see who placed which piece, and no hand labels were visible, so I'm not crediting building to anyone yet.

Maya: Strong collaborative leadership. She tracked everyone's progress, warned Priya to go gently at the lower pinch, and offered to take the lower curve or stay out of the way. Her offer was respectful and not pushy. Still no direct evidence of what she built; the sketch led to a working layout. Ask her and others what she placed.

Tom: Silent this visit. Leo said 'Thanks Tom', so Tom probably did something I missed, perhaps help or a tip. Top line is complete and connected, but I can't confirm he built it. Ask him.

Priya: Silent again. Maya says she was near the lower pinch, and the bottom line is connected and reaches the tail zone. Looks like solid execution but unverified. Ask her directly about her work, since she's quiet.

Leo: Owns the tail as one stroke. Declined Maya's offer to avoid collisions, but gave a clear, specific ask: close the gap where Priya's line stops short of the tail. That is good communication, though tail still open with about 7 min left.

Next visit: check whether the tail gap gets closed, who closes it, and whether anyone is bunching pieces or stalling. Collect who-placed-what accounts."}
